label: Weather, Temperature & Climate
labelVi: Thời tiết, Nhiệt độ & Khí hậu
descriptionVi: Từ vựng về điều kiện thời tiết, nắng, mưa, gió, mây, độ sáng và nhiệt độ.

passages.title: The Changing Seasons Across the Mountain Valley
passages.text: Living high in the alpine valley allows residents to observe dramatic shifts in weather throughout the rotating seasons. During early spring, a bright morning sun rises behind the snowy peaks, warming the cool mountain air. As the winter chill slowly fades, the sky turns brilliant blue, inviting outdoor hikers to explore nature trails. When summer arrives, the weather becomes noticeably hot and dry, turning the hillside meadows into golden pastures. Farmers welcome a gentle mountain wind that brings brief relief from the intense midday heat. On sheltered hillsides, cabins built on the lee slopes remain protected from sudden thunderstorm squalls. By late autumn, dark storm clouds frequently gather along the northern ridges as temperatures plunge. Icy gusts of wind begin to blow fiercely across the open valleys, shaking orange leaves from tall birch trees. When deep winter descends, frigid nights freeze the rushing river, turning surface water into sparkling solid ice. On still winter evenings, you can step outside into the crisp cold and admire each radiant star glowing brightly overhead. The North Star shines steadily against the black sky, guiding night travelers safely back toward village lights. Each shifting season brings distinct atmospheric rhythms that shape rural agricultural routines and daily outdoor life. Understanding local weather patterns helps villagers respect the power of nature and prepare thoughtfully for changing climates. Whether under a scorching afternoon sun or wrapped in winter snowfall, the mountain landscape retains timeless grandeur and serene peace. Embracing every changing breeze and sunny morning fosters deep appreciation for the natural wonders of our shared planet.

passages.title: Observing Weather Patterns and Seasonal Transitions Across the Year
passages.titleVi: Quan sát các hình thái thời tiết và sự chuyển mùa trong năm
passages.text: Observing daily weather patterns allows us to appreciate the dynamic beauty of changing seasons. In springtime, the air turns pleasantly warm, and bright morning sunshine streams across waking valleys. When summer arrives, days become predominantly sunny, although intense afternoon heat can make outdoor work exhausting. During midsummer, a sudden brief rain shower often cools down the baking earth, leaving fresh puddles along garden pathways. By late afternoon, a single white cloud might drift across the horizon before disappearing into the sunset. As autumn approaches, cooler temperatures arrive with overcast, cloudy mornings. Strong winds begin blowing fiercely through the orchards, causing red and gold leaves to go falling onto the damp grass. During this transition, a wet rainy week frequently settles over the valley, forcing families to spend cozy evenings indoors beside warm tea. In early mornings along the river, a dense foggy mist hangs low over the water, shrouding tree branches in mystery. When deep winter takes hold, the entire landscape transforms into a quiet snowy wonderland. Freezing winds sweep down from mountain ridges, yet people bundle up in woolen coats to enjoy the peaceful hush of snowfall. Understanding how weather shapes agriculture and daily routines reminds us that every season carries its own unique charm. Whether seeking shade from blistering heat or marveling at falling snow, we celebrate nature's timeless rhythms with joy and deep gratitude throughout our lives. Each shifting season brings distinct atmospheric rhythms that refresh our spirit and inspire mindful living. Villagers welcome sunny mornings and snowy afternoons alike as enduring blessings.

passages.title: Weather Transitions and Coastal Storm Resilience
passages.titleVi: Sự chuyển biến thời tiết và khả năng thích ứng với bão ven biển
passages.text: Living near the coastal shoreline provides daily opportunities to observe the dramatic forces of nature and changing weather rhythms. Early yesterday morning, the weather forecast indicated partly cloudy skies with a mild autumn temperature hovering around eighteen degrees. By noon, brilliant sunlight cast a radiant golden shine across the calm ocean waves, encouraging beach visitors to seek shade under colorful canvas umbrellas. However, meteorological stations soon issued an urgent advisory warning that a powerful tropical hurricane was churning rapidly toward the coast. Within hours, the atmospheric temperature plunged sharply as towering dark storm clouds rolled in from the horizon. Powerful gale-force gusts swept through coastal neighborhoods, leaving tall pine trees shaking violently against the fierce winds. Heavy torrential downpours battered windows, drenching street pavements and turning low-lying gardens into deep wet puddles. City emergency crews worked swiftly along the canal embankments to prevent a devastating river flood from inundating residential homes. Fortunately, by dawn the following morning, the ferocious ocean storm gradually subsided into gentle sea breezes. A single warm ray of morning sunlight pierced through retreating gray clouds, illuminating the resilient coastal town. Neighbors stepped outside to clear fallen tree branches and inspect neighborhood streets, relieved that careful community preparation had kept everyone safe. Understanding seasonal weather patterns helps coastal residents respect the powerful dynamics of nature and safeguard their communities against extreme weather events. Embracing both bright sunshine and turbulent storms teaches people to live in harmony with the natural environment. Furthermore, resilient community cooperation and dependable early warning systems ensure that families recover quickly whenever nature unleashes its most intense weather phenomena.

passages.title: Atmospheric Wonders and Seasonal Sky Gazing
passages.titleVi: Những kỳ quan khí quyển và việc ngắm bầu trời theo mùa
passages.text: Living near a high-altitude mountain observatory allows meteorologists and astronomy enthusiasts to observe remarkable atmospheric phenomena and dynamic seasonal climate transitions throughout the entire year. Each dawn, researchers greet the newly risen morning sun as its vibrant golden beams illuminate the surrounding misty alpine peaks and awakening valleys. Brilliant natural sunlight quickly warms the crisp mountain breeze, gradually dissolving the thick overnight fog that blankets the forest floor. During long daylight hours, the environmental research center operates entirely on clean electricity produced by high-capacity renewable solar panels and wind turbines. By midafternoon, intense summer heat and rising atmospheric humidity frequently trigger dramatic and rapid weather shifts across the rugged terrain. Dark, scattered rain clouds gather swiftly along the western canyon rim while atmospheric pressure drops noticeably within minutes. Soon, fierce windy conditions sweep across the open plateau, bending resilient evergreen trees and howling loudly past the protective metal observation domes. Sudden pouring torrents of cold rainwater drench the rocky ridges, washing mountain slopes and replenishing vital freshwater reservoirs across the valley below. Fortunately, these intense mountain storms pass just as swiftly, leaving washed skies and refreshing mountain air behind. When darkness settles, clear twilight skies reveal spectacular and pristine views of outer space without city light pollution. Last summer, astronomers hosted a memorable public viewing session during a rare total lunar eclipse, watching in awe as the moon turned a striking crimson hue. Months later, summit observatory telescopes recorded a radiant stellar nova sparkling brilliantly like a newly born diamond in a distant galaxy. Observing these awe-inspiring celestial wonders and powerful climate forces teaches students to appreciate the delicate balance of our global atmosphere and our enduring place in the vast universe.

passages.title: Monitoring Extreme Weather and Global Environmental Shifts
passages.titleVi: Theo dõi thời tiết cực đoan và những biến đổi môi trường toàn cầu
passages.text: In recent years, meteorologists worldwide have documented significant shifts in regional climate patterns. During the peak of midsummer, soaring atmospheric humidity frequently fuels sudden violent thunderstorm activity over coastal plains. Blinding downpours rapidly reduce roadway visibility to mere feet, creating hazardous driving conditions for daily commuters. Low-lying agricultural valleys were recently flooded when nearby rivers breached their earthen protective embankments. Such severe storm surges demonstrate how an unpredictable natural disaster can devastate rural infrastructure within hours. To protect vulnerable communities, emergency teams worked tirelessly to prevent contaminated floodwaters from infiltrating freshwater drinking reservoirs. Environmental researchers emphasize that global warming is accelerating the frequency and severity of extreme weather events. International agreements require industrialized nations to cut greenhouse gas emission rates from manufacturing plants and coal power stations. Deep inland, vast expanses of moist wetland ecosystems serve as natural sponges, absorbing excess runoff and regulating local temperatures. On hot summer afternoons, wisps of white steam rise gently from sunbaked riverbanks as water evaporates into the lower atmosphere. Promoting long-term ecological sustainability requires clean renewable energy sources, smarter agricultural land use, and robust water conservation policies. Local governments must invest in modernized storm drains and flood barriers to strengthen community resilience against changing precipitation trends. Educating young citizens about conservation fosters a collective commitment to protecting delicate planetary ecosystems. Through international scientific cooperation, humanity can develop innovative strategies to mitigate climate risks and secure a safer future for generations to come. Every individual action, from reducing household energy consumption to supporting green reforestation initiatives, contributes meaningfully to ecological restoration. Protecting our shared biosphere remains an urgent moral duty that unites communities across every continent and ocean.

passages.title: Surviving a Severe Tropical Storm on the Coastal Peninsula
passages.text: Early on an August morning, a gentle ocean breeze suddenly gives way to ominous changes across the coastal peninsula. Meteorologists issue urgent alerts warning that a severe tropical hurricane is forming over warm ocean waters. In the upper atmosphere, moisture condenses rapidly into a massive dark storm cloud that blocks out the midday sun. Industrial nitrogen oxide emissions in coastal cities can worsen air quality just before severe atmospheric pressure drops. Local authorities urge fishermen to secure their wooden boats firmly to harbor piers and advise homeowners to board up exterior glass windows. Within hours, the weather turns violent as torrential rain begins raining non-stop against residential windows. Fierce gusts whip across palm trees while blinding bolts of electrical lightning illuminate the gloomy horizon. A deafening roar of booming thunder shakes houses to their concrete foundations, prompting families to seek safety in interior hallways away from glass doors. Outside, low-lying streets quickly experience severe flooding as drainage canals overflow with muddy rainwater. Emergency response teams work courageously throughout the night to prevent widespread structural destruction across coastal neighborhoods. Civil defense officers monitor rising floodwaters and reinforce vulnerable embankments with sandbags. Community volunteers distribute bottled drinking water and dry blankets to families in emergency shelters. By daybreak, the ferocious tempest passes inland, allowing the sun to peek through dispersing clouds. Resilient residents step outside to assess damage and begin cleanup efforts together, demonstrating unity and strength after the intense storm. Mutual support and organized relief operations help neighborhoods restore power quickly and rebuild their infrastructure with improved storm resilience.
